blogs.title: When Pets Bite Back: Capnocytophaga canimorsus as an Unusual Trigger for Complement-Mediated HUS
blogs.description: This post reviews how a seemingly innocuous dog bite can seed a severe gram‑negative infection that progresses through septic shock into a complement‑mediated thrombotic microangiopathy (CM‑HUS). We break down the pathogen’s epidemiology, its slow growth yet aggressive systemic impact, and why clinicians should suspect it when unexplained pancytopenia or persistent coagulopathy follows a bite injury.

blogs.title: 'Beyond Sepsis-Induced DIC': Recognizing the Silent Onset of Microangiopathic Haemolysis
blogs.description: Early in critical illness sepsis masquerades behind DIC‐like laboratory findings—low fibrinogen, prolonged clotting times, thrombocytopenia—and masks microangiopathic damage. This article outlines the subtle clinical clues that signal transition into CM‑HUS once haemolysis emerges during recovery from shock, highlighting why repeated platelet counts and reticulocytosis beating are vital surveillance metrics.

blogs.title: "Fast‑Track TMA Work‑Up": ADAMTS13 Sauce Tip To Rule Out TTP Quickly
blogs.description: In an ICU scramble, distinguishing thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura from CM‑HUS determines whether plasma exchange or complement blockade is warranted. This piece walks readers through a pragmatic triage algorithm incorporating PLASMIC scoring at admission followed by rapid ADAMTS13 activity testing—illustrating how an intermediate value removes the suspicion of TTP while keeping options open.
